identity.name: Low-and-Slow Jittered C2 Beacon Behavioral Anomaly — Cortex Network Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1071 / T1571)
identity.summary: A host emits a periodic, low-and-slow trickle of small outbound sessions to one destination with sleep jitter — the Cobalt Strike / Sliver beacon profile. No domain or IP is a known-bad IOC; the deviation from the host's learned egress baseline (destination rarity, connection periodicity, small stable payload) is what an auto-tuned network ABIOC anchors on and fires on.
identity.description: Modern C2 frameworks such as Cobalt Strike (Malleable C2) and Sliver deliberately defeat static IOC matching: the operator rotates the callback domain/IP, tunes the sleep interval and adds jitter so the cadence looks irregular, and keeps each check-in small so it blends into ordinary web noise. A domain-blocklist or IOC rule keyed on a specific address therefore misses the beacon the moment infrastructure rotates. The signal that survives rotation is behavioral and lives entirely in the network plane: a single internal source repeatedly reaching one external destination at a near-constant interval (even with jitter the periodicity is statistically tight relative to normal browsing), with a small and stable per-request byte volume, to a destination that is rare for that host, sometimes over a non-standard port. Cortex Network Security Analytics learns each host's egress baseline — which destinations it talks to, at what cadence, with what payload profile — and PANW authors and continually auto-tunes Analytics Behavioral IOCs (ABIOCs) against that learned baseline, firing on a single suspicious flow that carries an identified chain of causality rather than on a known-bad indicator. This card exercises that detector class on the NDR plane. It injects two behavioral deviations from the learned host egress baseline: (a) a periodic low-and-slow beacon cadence with small stable payloads that diverges from the host's normal bursty, high-volume web traffic, and (b) a jittered beacon to a rare destination on a non-standard port that the host has never contacted at that cadence. Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL surfaces the periodicity and the rare-destination/non-standard-port deviation from panw_ngfw_traffic_raw; and a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single C2-beacon incident anchored to the host egress causality chain (rare destination -> periodic small sessions -> jittered cadence), which a static domain/IOC rule would never have raised.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-NDR-008 — Low-and-slow jittered C2 beacon behavioral deviation from a learned host egress baseline for Cortex network ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: NGFW inline with Enhanced Application Logs forwarding into XSIAM so per-session egress telemetry reaches panw_ngfw_traffic_raw.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the source host produced only its normal egress so Cortex Network Security Analytics learned the host egress profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad IOC. Emit a periodic low-and-slow beacon that deviates from the
# host's learned egress baseline (destination rarity + tight periodicity + small
# stable payload), then a jittered beacon to a rare destination on a non-standard port.
set -euo pipefail
for i in $(seq 1 12); do curl -s --max-time 3 http://${BEACON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/beacon >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 2; done
for i in $(seq 1 8); do curl -s --max-time 3 http://${BEACON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:8443/task >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 3; done

input_variables.name: BEACON_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised internal host the low-and-slow beacon reaches during the deviation.

expected_artifacts.description: Repeated small outbound sessions from one source to a single destination at a near-constant low-and-slow interval that diverges from the host's learned egress baseline.
A jittered beacon to a destination that is rare for the host, over a non-standard port the host has never used at that cadence.

abiocs.name: NDR-008 Periodic Low-and-Slow Beacon Deviating from Host Egress Baseline
abiocs.description: A source host that Cortex has learned emits bursty, high-volume web traffic suddenly produces a tight, periodic trickle of small sessions to a single destination — the Cobalt Strike / Sliver low-and-slow beacon shape. Every destination is legitimate-looking and rotates, so no IOC matches; the ABIOC fires on the periodicity-and-small-payload deviation from the host's learned egress baseline, anchored to the destination causality chain rather than to a known-bad indicator.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "http", "ssl", "unknown-tcp")
| filter action = "allow"
| comp count() as beacon_count, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes, count_distinct(uri) as uri_variants by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter beacon_count >= 8 and avg_bytes < 2048
| sort desc beacon_count
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, beacon_count, avg_bytes, uri_variants
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host egress baseline (bursty, high-volume, many destinations) -> a single rare destination contacted at a tight periodic interval with small stable payloads, anchored to the originating source host.

abiocs.name: NDR-008 Jittered Beacon to Rare Destination With Non-Standard Port Deviation
abiocs.description: A host contacts a destination that is rare for it over a non-standard port at a jittered but still statistically periodic cadence — the sleep-with-jitter profile Malleable C2 and Sliver use to evade fixed-interval rules. The ABIOC fires on the rare-destination-plus-non-standard-port deviation from the learned baseline, anchored to the periodic beacon that spawned the flows, catching the beacon after infrastructure rotation defeats any IOC.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter action = "allow"
| filter dst_port not in (80, 443, 53)
| comp count() as sessions, count_distinct(dst_ip) as dst_cardinality, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes by src_ip, dst_host, dst_port
| filter sessions >= 6 and dst_cardinality = 1 and avg_bytes < 2048
| sort desc sessions
| fields src_ip, dst_host, dst_port, sessions, dst_cardinality, avg_bytes
abiocs.causality_anchor: Periodic low-and-slow beacon under the source host -> a rare destination reached on a non-standard port the host never used at that cadence, anchored to the beacon flow that generated the sessions.

xql_queries.name: NDR-008 Beacon Periodicity Surfaced Against Host Egress Baseline
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "http", "ssl", "unknown-tcp")
| filter action = "allow"
| comp count() as beacon_count, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter beacon_count >= 8 and avg_bytes < 2048
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, beacon_count, avg_bytes

xql_queries.name: NDR-008 Rare Destination and Non-Standard Port Deviation Surfaced
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter action = "allow"
| filter dst_port not in (80, 443, 53)
| comp count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_host, dst_port
| filter sessions >= 6
| fields src_ip, dst_host, dst_port, sessions

correlation_rules.name: Low-and-Slow C2 Beacon Behavioral Anomaly — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(NDR-008 Periodic Low-and-Slow Beacon Deviating from Host Egress Baseline) AND ABIOC(NDR-008 Jittered Beacon to Rare Destination With Non-Standard Port Deviation) — fuses the two auto-tuned network behavioral deviations for the same source host into a single low-and-slow C2 beacon incident anchored to the host egress causality chain, surviving destination/IP rotation that defeats any static IOC.

threat_scenarios.name: Low-and-Slow C2 Beacon Behavioral Anomaly Detection via Cortex Network ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Network Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a host's egress baseline and detect a jittered low-and-slow beacon by its periodicity, small stable payload, destination rarity and non-standard port deviation, anchored to the host egress causality chain, after infrastructure rotation defeats any static IOC.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex learns the host egress baseline and an injected low-and-slow jittered beacon fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: NGFW inline with EAL forwarding to XSIAM (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw populated).
Baseline window elapsed with the source host producing only its normal egress.
steps: Let the host egress baseline window elapse.
Emit a periodic low-and-slow beacon, then a jittered beacon to a rare destination on a non-standard port.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-NDR-0008 raise a low-and-slow C2 beacon incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `NDR-008 Periodic Low-and-Slow Beacon Deviating from Host Egress Baseline` fires.
ABIOC `NDR-008 Jittered Beacon to Rare Destination With Non-Standard Port Deviation` fires.
Correlation CR-NDR-0008 raises one stitched low-and-slow C2 beacon incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce App-ID least-privilege egress and require an authenticated egress proxy so servers cannot reach arbitrary destinations or non-standard ports directly.
Block newly-registered / high-entropy domains and deny outbound to non-standard ports on egress NGFW policy so beacon channels are cut, not merely detected.
Apply Advanced Threat Prevention and URL Filtering on all outbound web traffic.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune network ABIOCs against the learned per-host egress baseline rather than hand-authoring IOC rules for individual C2 domains that rotate.
Baseline per-host destination cardinality, inter-request interval and payload profile; alert on low-jitter periodic small sessions to a rare destination.
Alert on egress to a non-standard port for a host whose baseline never used it, and correlate periodicity + rare-destination + non-standard-port into one C2 incident.
